subject: POC onramp: hosting options, eval success criteria & owners
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Allison Park <apark@atlashealth.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: POC onramp: hosting options, eval success criteria & owners

Hi Allison / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of hosting options we discussed (pros/cons at a glance)
- Hosted (Redwood API sandbox): fastest to spin up, lowest ops friction, not ideal if you need customer-managed networking or PHI isolation.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, better isolation for higher-volume tests, more lead time for capacity.
- VPC trial (private deployment): full network isolation and KMS integration; typical for workloads with PHI or strict compliance.

Suggested success criteria for the POC (please confirm / adjust):
- Latency: p95 generation <= 600ms for 512-token prompts (measured over sample traffic).
- Throughput: sustained 30 tokens/s in peak batch tests.
- Relevancy: embedding retrieval MAP >= 0.82 on provided eval set (we can run blind eval).
- Cost target: incremental inference cost <= $0.015 per 1k tokens (target to compare to internal baseline).
- Security: SOC 2 evidence and certs reviewed; if PHI is in scope, VPC preferred.

High-level timeline (proposed):
- Wed 5/26: finalize hosting choice & sign SOW (DocuSign).
- Mon 6/01: kickoff + data ingestion window opens.
- Week of 6/08: run baseline eval & latency/throughput sanity checks.
- 6/15–6/26: 2-week live trial with agreed traffic patterns + quality checks.
- 6/29: wrap / results review and decision meeting.

Owners (we can adjust):
- Sales / commercial: Ben Carter (point of contact for contract & timeline).
- Trial orchestration: Marissa Cole (trial coordinator, monitoring & dashboards).
- Infrastructure sizing & cost estimate: Karthik Iyer (infra lead).
- Security & evidence: Monica Patel (security questionnaire + evidence collection).

Attachments included: Atlas_SOW_template.docx (SOW draft), trial_environment_checklist.pdf (quick ops checklist).

Please reply with any edits to the success criteria, your hosting preference (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC), and whether the proposed kickoff window looks OK. Once you confirm hosting we will lock infra sizing and final SOW terms.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Allison Park <apark@atlashealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Harris <tharris@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC onramp: hosting options, eval success criteria & owners

Ben — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

1) Hosting preference: Because we'll be importing deidentified PHI extracts for testing, our security/compliance team will likely push for a VPC trial. If that's not feasible within your proposed timeline, dedicated sandbox with customer KMS would be our second choice. Hosted sandbox is our last resort given compliance constraints.

2) Success criteria tweaks:
- Latency: p95 <= 500–600ms is good — we expect your measurements to be taken with our sample prompts and 95th percentile across peak windows.
- Relevancy / retrieval: we'd prefer a threshold of embedding similarity > 0.85 on our gold set; happy for you to run the blind eval but please share the evaluation harness.
- Error tolerance: max 2% malformed outputs for structured responses (we'll send sample templates).

3) Security: our security team will send a standard evidence request to security@redwood.ai — SOC 2 report + encryption-in-transit docs + data retention policy are must-haves. Monica, you'll probably be looped in.

4) Timeline: a 6-week trial is realistic for us (data prep + phased traffic ramp). If we can agree on a 6/01 kickoff we can meet the 6/29 review date you suggested.

I'll attach a short internal checklist (we'll send formally in a separate email). For now, please confirm which hosting option you recommend given our PHI note, and whether Redwood can support KMS in Dedicated or VPC by kickoff.

Thanks,
Allison Park
Head of Product, Atlas Health
apark@atlashealth.com

If Atlas needs a faster start and can accept customer-managed KMS without full VPC, Dedicated sandbox is an acceptable compromise. We'll confirm exact lead times after Karthik's sizing note.

2) Security evidence: Monica will post the SOC2 and encryption docs to the shared drive and reply to security@redwood.ai by Tue 5/25.

3) Evaluation harness and metrics: Marissa will drop the evaluation harness into the shared folder (blind scoring). We'll run the embedding similarity and provide per-run reports. We can target embedding similarity > 0.85 as a pass threshold but recommend a qualitative review as well.

4) Timeline & next calendar items:
- Tue 5/25: Monica & Karthik deliver evidence bundle + sizing.
- Wed 5/26: Final hosting decision & DocuSign SOW (if commercial ok).
- Mon 6/01: Target kickoff (data ingest window opens).

5) Commercial note: I'll prepare a conditional SOW that covers both Dedicated and VPC options to keep signing friction low — we will attach the exact hosting addendum after Karthik confirms lead time and cost delta.
